title: The Gnat and the Bull

full_text:
A tiny gnat, having buzzed around the meadow for an entire afternoon, grew weary from his flight and decided to rest. He landed softly upon the tip of one of the massive horns of a colossal prize bull that was grazing peacefully in the pasture.

The gnat groomed his wings, cleaned his microscopic antennae, and rested for an hour while the great beast munched sweet clover, totally unaware of the insect's presence.

When the gnat was refreshed and prepared to take flight, he felt an overwhelming surge of self-importance. He buzzed loudly in the bull's ear and said with grand, pompous courtesy: "Noble beast, I have rested upon your horn long enough. I thank you for your hospitality! I must depart now, but if my weight has burdened your brow, I beg your pardon for the inconvenience."

The colossal bull did not even interrupt his chewing. He slowly raised one lazy eye toward his horn, exhaled a warm gust of steam through his nostrils, and replied in a deep, rumbling voice:

"Little fellow, do not trouble yourself with apologies. To tell you the honest truth, I did not even know you had arrived, and I shall certainly not notice when you are gone!"

Mortified by the giant's indifference, the tiny gnat buzzed away into the weeds, his swollen vanity deflated by the truth of his absolute insignificance.
moral: The smaller the mind, the greater the conceit; you are not as important as you imagine.
